sentences.text: Liaoxipterus is a pterodactyloid pterosaur known from a crushed mandible measuring 161 millimetres in length, which bears only eleven short teeth on each side.
Its upper jaw was rounded and packed with small, peg-like teeth.
The species name brachyognathus translates to "short jaw" in Greek.
Researchers suggest this animal was an insect eater that may have protruded its tongue like a chameleon to catch prey.
The genus name Liaoxipterus combines the discovery locality Liaoxi with the Greek word for wing.
Wang and colleagues suggested in 2006 and 2008 that Liaoxipterus belonged to the family Istiodactylidae, a view accepted by Lü in 2015.
Liaoxipterus lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
